questions.prompt: Since the allies could not defend themselves, they sent envoys to Caesar.
questions.answer: Sociī cum sē dēfendere nōn possent, lēgātōs ad Caesarem mīsērunt.

questions.prompt: Having removed the horses from sight, the general encouraged his men and joined battle.
questions.answer: Dux equīs ex cōnspectū remōtīs suōs cohortātus proelium commīsit.

questions.prompt: When the citizens had taken up arms, they attacked the camp of the enemy by night.
questions.answer: Cīvēs cum arma sūmpsissent, castra hostium noctū oppugnāvērunt.

questions.prompt: When the leader had crossed the river, he pitched camp on the higher bank.
questions.answer: Dux cum flūmen trānsiisset, in altiōre rīpā castra posuit.

questions.prompt: Although the sailors were tortured by fear, they steered the ship through the storm.
questions.answer: Nautae quamquam metū cruciābantur, nāvem per tempestātem gubernābant.

questions.prompt: Having veiled her face, the maiden entered the temple in silence.
questions.answer: Virgō vultū vēlātō templum tacita intrāvit.

questions.prompt: Since he judged the plan to be too little safe, the consul put off the battle.
questions.answer: Cōnsul cum cōnsilium parum tūtum esse arbitrārētur, proelium distulit.

questions.prompt: Although he was burning with love, the young man hid his wound with a calm face.
questions.answer: Adulēscēns quamquam amōre flagrābat, vulnus vultū tranquillō cēlābat.

questions.prompt: When the enemy had been driven from the walls, the townsmen added wood to the fires.
questions.answer: Oppidānī cum hostēs ā moenibus pulsī essent, lignum ignibus addidērunt.

questions.prompt: Having conquered the enemy, the victorious general returned to the city in triumph.
questions.answer: Imperātor hostibus victīs victor in urbem cum triumphō rediit.

questions.prompt: Since the actor feared the tragedy would displease the people, he changed the ending.
questions.answer: Histriō cum tragoediam populō displicēre timēret, fīnem mūtāvit.

questions.prompt: When the storm had been calmed, the sailors resumed their course toward the harbor.
questions.answer: Nautae cum tempestās sēdāta esset, cursum ad portum resūmpsērunt.

questions.prompt: Although they were worn out by the long siege, the citizens refused to surrender themselves.
questions.answer: Cīvēs quamquam longā obsidiōne fessī erant, sē dēdere recūsāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Having appeased the angry general, the envoys returned safe to the camp.
questions.answer: Lēgātī īrātō ducē plācātō tūtī in castra rediērunt.

questions.prompt: Since the guest despised the banquet, he mocked the verses of the host.
questions.answer: Hospes cum convīvium contemneret, versiculōs dominī irrīsit.

questions.prompt: Since the soldiers could not endure hunger, they surrendered the camp to the enemy.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs cum famem tolerāre nōn possent, castra hostibus trādidērunt.

questions.prompt: Since the merchant had lost his money, he sought help from his friends.
questions.answer: Mercātor cum nummōs āmīsisset, auxilium ab amīcīs petīvit.

questions.prompt: Although the priest was weary with long toil, he approached the sacred altar.
questions.answer: Sacerdōs quamquam longō labōre fessus erat, ad sacrum altāre accessit.

questions.prompt: When the citizens had heard the news, they ran together into the forum.
questions.answer: Cīvēs ubi nūntium audīvērunt, in forum concurrērunt.

questions.prompt: Although the boy was wandering in the shady wood, he did not fear the wild beasts.
questions.answer: Puer quamquam in silvā opācā aberrābat, ferās nōn timēbat.

questions.prompt: Since the poet had discovered a hidden treasure, he sang joyful songs.
questions.answer: Poēta cum thēsaurum occultum invēnisset, laeta carmina cecinit.

questions.prompt: Although the envoys feared the enemy, they boldly delivered the message.
questions.answer: Lēgātī quamquam hostem timēbant, mandātum audācter nūntiāvērunt.

questions.prompt: When winter had come, the shepherd led his flock down into the valley.
questions.answer: Pāstor ubi hiems vēnerat, gregem in vallem dūxit.

questions.prompt: Since the consul was seeking peace, he sent gifts to the fierce king.
questions.answer: Cōnsul cum pācem peteret, dōna ad rēgem ferōcem mīsit.

questions.prompt: When the general had learned what was happening in the camp, he ordered the legions to advance.
questions.answer: Cum imperātor cognōvisset quid in castrīs gererētur, legiōnēs prōgredī iussit.

questions.prompt: Since the magician could not appease the angry crowd, he fled from the tribunal by night.
questions.answer: Magus cum turbam īrātam plācāre nōn posset, nocte ā tribūnālī fūgit.

questions.prompt: Although the disciple was worn out by long study, he approached the master with joy.
questions.answer: Discipulus etsī longō studiō dēfessus erat, tamen ad magistrum laetus accessit.

questions.prompt: After the poet had recited these verses, he set out from the city.
questions.answer: Postquam poēta hōs versūs recitāvit, ex urbe profectus est.

questions.prompt: When this had been announced to the consul, he hastened to leave the province.
questions.answer: Cōnsul, cum hoc eī nūntiātum esset, prōvinciā excēdere mātūrāvit.

questions.prompt: Since a reward had been promised to the soldiers, they attacked the walls more fiercely.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, cum praemium eīs prōmissum esset, mūrōs ācrius oppugnāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Although a day of trial had been appointed for the leader, he despised the threats of the people.
questions.answer: Dux etsī eī diēs dicta esset, tamen minās populī contempsit.

questions.prompt: When a wound had been inflicted on the gladiator, the crowd fell silent.
questions.answer: Gladiātōrī cum vulnus illātum esset, turba conticuit.

questions.prompt: The consul, lest he be forced to spend the winter in the mountains, ordered the army to hurry.
questions.answer: Cōnsul, nē in montibus hiemem cōnsūmere cōgerētur, exercitum contendere iussit.

questions.prompt: The magician, in order to take away hope of escape, hid the keys of the gate.
questions.answer: Magus, ut spem fugae tolleret, portae clāvēs abscondit.

questions.prompt: The queen, so that she might soften the anger of the king, sent many gifts.
questions.answer: Rēgīna, ut rēgis īram mollīret, multa dōna mīsit.

questions.prompt: Theseus, in order that he might find the way back, unrolled a thread through the dark halls.
questions.answer: Thēseus, ut viam regrediendī invenīret, per obscūrās aulās fīlum ēvolvit.

questions.prompt: It happened that on a single night all the statues were thrown down.
questions.answer: Accidit ut ūnā nocte omnia signa dēicerentur.

questions.prompt: So great was the storm that the sailors despaired of safety.
questions.answer: Tanta erat tempestās ut nautae dē salūte dēspērārent.

questions.prompt: The general asked the scouts what the enemy were doing beyond the river.
questions.answer: Imperātor explōrātōrēs rogāvit quid hostēs trāns flūmen agerent.

questions.prompt: No one knew how great the danger was that threatened the city.
questions.answer: Nēmō sciēbat quantum perīculum urbī impendēret.

questions.prompt: If anyone should trust the magician, he would be a fool.
questions.answer: Sī quis magō crēdat, stultus sit.

questions.prompt: Although the danger had been made equal, hope of flight was taken from all.
questions.answer: Etsī perīculum aequātum erat, spēs fugae omnibus adēmpta est.

questions.prompt: If the frugality of the citizens had been greater, the treasury would not have been exhausted.
questions.answer: Sī cīvium parsimōnia māior fuisset, aerārium nōn exhaustum esset.

questions.prompt: Although the origanum was bitter, the physician mixed it into the drink.
questions.answer: Etsī orīganum amārum erat, medicus illud pōtiōnī admiscuit.

questions.prompt: Having pitched camp, the general, since he feared an ambush, ordered the watches to be increased.
questions.answer: Castrīs positīs, imperātor, cum īnsidiās timēret, vigiliās augērī iussit.

questions.prompt: When the signal had been given, the soldiers, in order to break the enemy's line, charged with drawn swords.
questions.answer: Signō datō, mīlitēs, ut aciem hostium perrumperent, strictīs gladiīs impetum fēcērunt.

questions.prompt: The magician, having veiled the tribunal in smoke, so terrified the people that all fled.
questions.answer: Magus, tribūnālī fūmō obtēctō, populum ita terruit ut omnēs fugerent.

questions.prompt: After the king had been slain, the citizens, so that they might restore liberty, appointed two consuls.
questions.answer: Rēge interfectō, cīvēs, ut lībertātem restituerent, duōs cōnsulēs creāvērunt.

questions.prompt: Although the king had promised peace, he was secretly preparing war.
questions.answer: Rēx quamquam pācem prōmīserat, tamen bellum clam parābat.

questions.prompt: When the general had drawn up his battle line, he ordered the trumpets to sound.
questions.answer: Dux, cum aciem īnstrūxisset, tubās canere iussit.

questions.prompt: If anyone should despise the laws, he would harm the whole state.
questions.answer: Sī quis lēgēs contemnat, tōtī cīvitātī noceat.

questions.prompt: It happened that in a single winter many temples were destroyed by fire.
questions.answer: Accidit ut ūnā hieme multa templa igne dēstruerentur.

questions.prompt: The envoys, since they could not persuade the senate, returned home in sorrow.
questions.answer: Lēgātī, cum senātuī persuādēre nōn possent, maestī domum rediērunt.

questions.prompt: The commander, when the ambush had been reported to him, ordered the cavalry to halt.
questions.answer: Imperātor, cum īnsidiae eī nūntiātae essent, equitēs cōnsistere iussit.

questions.prompt: Having seized the hill, the soldiers, because they feared the enemy, fortified the camp with a rampart.
questions.answer: Mīlitēs, colle occupātō, quod hostēs timēbant, castra vallō mūnīvērunt.

questions.prompt: Although the leader had once saved the city, the citizens drove him into exile.
questions.answer: Ducem, quamquam urbem ōlim servāverat, cīvēs in exsilium ēgērunt.

questions.prompt: The consul, lest the enemy escape by night, stationed guards at the gates.
questions.answer: Cōnsul, nē hostēs nocte effugerent, custōdēs ad portās collocāvit.

questions.prompt: After the poet had recited his verses, the crowd applauded with a great shout.
questions.answer: Postquam poēta versūs recitāvit, turba magnō clāmōre plausit.

questions.prompt: So great was the storm that the ships could not leave the harbor.
questions.answer: Tanta erat tempestās ut nāvēs portū ēgredī nōn possent.

questions.prompt: The old man asked why the young men were neglecting their studies.
questions.answer: Senex rogāvit cūr iuvenēs studia neglegerent.

questions.prompt: If there is any hope in the allies — and I know how small it is — we must fight.
questions.answer: Sī qua est in sociīs spēs, quam sciō quam sit exigua, pugnandum est.

questions.prompt: The enemy, after they had sent men to discover the plans of the Romans, withdrew into the woods.
questions.answer: Hostēs, cum hominēs mīsissent quī cōnsilia Rōmānōrum cognōscerent, in silvās sē recēpērunt.

questions.prompt: Although the farmer perceived why the fields were barren, he sowed the seeds again.
questions.answer: Agricola etsī intellegēbat quā dē causā agrī sterilēs essent, tamen sēmina iterum sēvit.

questions.prompt: Having freed the captives, the victorious king, in order to win their loyalty, gave them gifts.
questions.answer: Rēx victor, captīvīs līberātīs, ut eōrum fidem sibi conciliāret, dōna eīs dedit.
